scene.title: This output is close but not quite right
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Week 2 – "This output is close but not quite right"

Maya asked Claude to draft a quarterly client summary. The first version was too long, used the wrong tone, and missed a key metric. She tried rewording the prompt eight times. Versions 6, 7, and 8 all had the same flaw: the executive summary buried the bottom line three paragraphs down.

Her colleague asked, "Did you tell Claude what was wrong and what you needed instead?" Maya had been guessing at prompt changes without diagnosing the specific problem. She learned the diagnose-revise-verify loop: pinpoint the flaw, fix it with a targeted follow-up, then check whether it worked.

takeaways: Refinement runs in order: diagnose the specific weakness, revise with a targeted fix, verify it worked, then decide what's next.
Three consecutive near-identical outputs with the same flaw means diminishing returns: stop prompting, edit by hand or change approach.
Productive feedback responses: map each reviewer comment to a specific change, and ask clarifying questions when feedback is ambiguous.
Disciplined iteration fixes only what reviewers flagged: leave accepted parts alone, don't rewrite from scratch or add unrequested changes.
